title: Scheduler thaw and circuit-breaker to unblock tenant queues during rolling upgrades
creator: Lena Gomez
description: Several customers reported intermittent severe p99 tail latency for short requests and apparent queue starvation after we rolled runtime upgrades in Private and Dedicated clusters. Investigation shows a state mismatch between batcher admission windows and prefetch/eviction heuristics during rolling upgrades which can shrink effective admission for short requests, causing long-context flows to dominate and starve latency-sensitive traffic. This ticket implements a coordinated "thaw" mechanism plus a lightweight circuit-breaker to restore and protect admission capacity during rolling upgrades and similar transient state transitions.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Marcus Chen: Initial investigation: reproduced at scale in staging by simulating a rolling upgrade that restarts worker processes and toggles KV cache population. Observed admission_window drop from 64 -> 8 while inflight long-context batches stayed high. Short requests queue length spikes ~7x. Captured logs and traces (link in dashboards).

2026-03-04 - Aisha Patel (on-call SE): Customer 'AcmePayments' raised a Sev2 after scheduled Dedicated upgrade; provided timeline and trace IDs. Notified SRE and product. Temporary mitigation: manually increased admission_window on affected hosts — improved p99 short-request latency immediately.

2026-03-06 - Marcus Chen: PoC: add 'thaw token' that is emitted by the coordinator on process start/upgrade completion. Token triggers admission recalibration and resets prefetch reservation hysteresis for 30s. Validated in local perf harness with mixed workload (10% long-context, 90% short). p99 short-request latency drop from 280ms -> 55ms during window.

2026-03-09 - QA (Diego Ruiz): Integration tests added to long-context-simulator. Two failure cases discovered: 1) thaw token retries caused duplicate KV prefetch thrash, 2) some older private hosts didn't accept token due to API version mismatch. Added compatibility handler and backoff for prefetch.

2026-03-11 - Marcus Chen: Implemented circuit-breaker on prefetch and admission shrink path: if admission_window falls >50% within 10s, stop prefetch eviction churn and hold a conservative reservation for short flows. Adds metrics that surface the event. Preparing PR.

2026-03-13 - PM (Riya Nair): Communicated mitigation and interim opt-out to affected enterprise customers and added post-update checklist to Private upgrade runbook. Scheduled canary rollout for runtime-1.19 with thaw/circuit-breaker enabled by default for Hosted and Dedicated canaries.

2026-03-14 - Marcus Chen: PR opened and running CI. Need approvals from SRE and Runtime SIG. Also planned a 24h canary with real traffic and automated rollback if short-request p99 increases >25% over baseline.
root_cause: During rolling restarts, the local admission controller recomputed admission windows using stale occupancy metrics while prefetch eviction heuristics aggressively reclaimed KV cache memory. The recomputed admission sometimes collapsed for short requests, allowing ongoing long-context batches to occupy most slots and causing starvation for latency-sensitive traffic.
fix_summary: 1) Introduce a coordinator-issued 'thaw token' post-start that triggers a controlled admission-window recalibration and temporarily increases short-request reservation. 2) Add a lightweight circuit-breaker that detects rapid admission shrink and suspends aggressive prefetch-eviction for a short grace period. 3) Add compatibility backoff for older private agent versions and a fallback conservative admission policy.
rollout_plan: Canary 1: Hosted small region (10% hosts) - enable thaw/circuit-breaker - 24h monitoring
Canary 2: Dedicated reserved capacity pools - 10% traffic - 24h
Canary 3: Private customers on opt-in runtime-1.19 image - coordinate with SRE/SEs
Full rollout: 100% after two successful canaries and no regressions for 48h
test_plan: Add deterministic long-context + short-request mixed workload in perf harness with variable restart patterns
Regression test: repeated rolling restart simulation with KV cache cold/warm cycles (100 iterations)
Chaos test: randomized worker restarts under production-like ingress wavefronts
E2E: run canary against real traffic with automated p50/p95/p99 guards
customer_reports: AcmePayments (Enterprise) - reported recurring spikes after scheduled Dedicated upgrade
Learnly (SaaS) - intermittent short-request timeouts during Private runtime patching
FinMuse (Financial) - elevated p99 for inference endpoints during mixed-length waves
resolution_summary: Implemented thaw token and circuit-breaker; validated in staging perf harness and on two canaries. Short-request p99 returned to baseline in canaries. Private agent compatibility fixes added. Preparing full rollout pending SRE approvals and 48h no-regression window.
